findings.title: _written treats every RuntimeError (NotImplementedError included) as 'the account moved while it was serialized', so a spend recorded in a state that fails to serialize every time is never observed, and a restore re-dispatches the executed action
findings.evidence: src/engcore/mind/world/owners.py:111-121. `except RecursionError` gives _Unreadable; then `except RuntimeError as exc: raise OwnerUnavailable(f"{what} moved while it was serialized")`, a refusal for that verification only, which is never recorded in _diverged (owners.py:450-459). NotImplementedError subclasses RuntimeError (checked in this session). The ledger path calls canonical_digest's json.dumps(..., default=str) inside _written (owners.py:378-379), so str() of any non-JSON charge field runs there. README §9:500-503 says that refusing for good an unwritable handed state 'also closes the pre-existing class of unwritable spends'. §4:175-177 and owners.py:325-328 state that a state its owner cannot write down refuses its account from then on.
findings.reproduction: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-forge/e352a8b8-4d77-5787-bd23-1bcc1dda83b7/scratchpad/review_r11/A-scientific-authority/a1104_runtimeerror_class_hides_spend.py, run from /home/user/forge at aad2f69. The executor settles a charge whose detail is an object whose __str__ raises NotImplementedError. Result: after the spend 'OwnerUnavailable: ... moved while it was serialized'; after an object-replacing restore 'DISPATCHED AGAIN; executor calls 2'. The same sequence with __str__ raising TypeError: refused for good, restore refused, executor calls 1. The same gap exists for experiments through a nested dict subclass whose items() raises a RuntimeError subclass. The c69e579 and ceaf8cd code paths, read but not executed on those trees, also refused it per verification only, so round 10 left this rather than introduced it.
findings.why: This is the R10-C-F1 outcome (a handed spend is never observed, then a rollback re-authorizes the executed action), in a sub-class round 10's fix leaves open. The reader decides 'moving' versus 'unwritable' from the exception type, and that type does not say whether the state moved. It is rated MINOR, not MAJOR, because the trigger is an execution-side value in a str-typed owner field whose own conversion deterministically raises a RuntimeError subclass. No owner code (scientific core, sria.campaign) raises RuntimeError, and at-most-once execution is a documented residual. It still keeps Q4 PARTIAL: it is a narrow, demonstrated bypass of the follower's forward-only budget-currency guarantee.
findings.fix: Classify by behaviour, not by exception type. Serialize the account a second time. If the two attempts differ, or one succeeds, the state moved (refused for this verification only). If both fail the same way, the state is _Unreadable (refused for good). Alternatively, limit the carve-out to the interpreter's 'changed size during iteration' RuntimeError. Add a1104 (both the ledger detail and the experiment dict-subclass forms) as a control. Otherwise, restate README §4/§9 and owners.py:325-330 to say that an unwritable state whose serialization raises a RuntimeError subclass is not observed.

Neither path asks whether the failure came from the state or from the moment of the read. The README and docstring claim otherwise: README section 4:178 says 'Concurrent verifications never refuse for good an account that only moved forward'; owners.py:326-328 and README section 4:189/:199 say 'a state that moved while it was serialized is refused for that verification only'. A ledger has no torn-read check at all: owners.py:378-383 compares nothing that was written with what was read back, unlike the experiment path at :403.

CASE=experiment: an exhausted experiment gets a new ExperimentBudget(3) and one more observation is recorded. The torn text holds the old budget and the new evaluation, so from_dict raises 'observation budget exhausted' and the account is refused for good. The same probe on a c69e579 tree copy: both verifications are refused once and served afterwards, so this is a round-10 regression. findings.question: Q4
findings.title: Round 10 refuses for good an honest account that moved forward while it was serialized: a concurrent top-up and record make the owner's from_dict reject the torn text, and that failure counts as 'unwritable'
findings.evidence: src/engcore/mind/world/owners.py:110-121: _written decides by exception type. RecursionError and any non-RuntimeError become _Unreadable; any other RuntimeError is OwnerUnavailable, meaning 'moved'. owners.py:397-402: ScientificExperiment.from_dict(json.loads(text_)) runs BEFORE the torn-accounting check at owners.py:403-405, and any failure there raises _Unreadable. owners.py:420-421 and 450-456 then store it in _diverged for good. The docs say otherwise: README.md:178 'Concurrent verifications never refuse for good an account that only moved forward'; README.md:188-189 and owners.py:326-328 'a state that moved while it was serialized is refused for that verification only'. owners.py:311-312 also call a top-up 'a move of the owner'. Probe d20 (settrace-forced, deterministic): (a) a ledger's total is read before an honest two-step top-up (total+100, then a reservation of total+50) and its reservation after it. Result: FOR GOOD with 'reserved validation budget exceeds the total budget', at every later verification. The ledger is now 110/60 and readable by its owner, a new reader reads it, and admission through the old reader is MISSING_INFORMATION AUTHORITY_OWNER_UNAVAILABLE. (b) An exhausted experiment's budget is written before a top-up plus record and its evaluations after. Result: FOR GOOD with 'observation budget exhausted (20)'. The account now has 21 observations within a budget of 25, and a new reader reads revision 21. Probe d20c (real threads, no tracing, default switch interval 0.005 s): 3 refusals for good after 3890 reads. The account is then readable by its owner (274 attempts) and by a new reader. d20b: the ledger variant is not reachable with real threads on GIL CPython 3.13 (0 of 3000), because the declaration attributes are loaded with no call between them. No control covers this: mutants torn_for_good (owners.py:404 raises _Unreadable) and runtime_for_good (owners.py:119 raises _Unreadable) each passed the whole BR1.1 suite (611 passed, 1 skipped = BR1 git-only test) in an aad2f69 tree copy. tests/mind/test_authority_review_r8.py:124 uses a non-following reader and matches only the message; r6:75 swaps whole objects, so it never tears.

Mutants: mutants.py <tree> torn_for_good | runtime_for_good, then the item-1 suite from the tree root.
findings.why: This is new in round 10 (round 9 refused every read-back failure for that verification only). An honest execution side that tops up an observation budget while proposer threads verify loses the account for good. Every admission bound to it is then refused until a new reader is built, which contradicts two stated guarantees. It fails closed and admits nothing wrong, so it is MINOR. It is a liveness defect plus a false behaviour claim, with no regression control on either 'this verification only' path.
findings.fix: Decide 'moved' by observing movement, not by exception class. When a read-back fails, write the account down again. Refuse for good only if the second write gives byte-identical text that fails the same way (or raises the same error type and message). Otherwise refuse for this verification only. Alternatively, run the torn checks on the parsed written text (budget/accounting against the written evaluations) before calling from_dict. Add d20's settrace interleaving as a deterministic control on a following reader: the torn verification is refused and the next one reads. Add a following-reader control for the accounting tear and for a RuntimeError while serializing, both asserting not 'from then on'.
